title: Tartaria
subtitle: Test your grasp of Tartaria — free-energy civilization, Mud-floods, Tuning Forks, Atmospheric Condensers, Orphan Trains, and the 8th Re-set trajectory.

reflection.title: Reflection
reflection.body: Tartaria was not a myth — it was worldwide free-energy excellence murdered by a planned Re-set. Mud-floods buried the bones of that world. Tuning forks turned stone to putty. Domes sang ether. Condensers rode Ley Lines until coal melted them. Giants vaulted by the Smithsonian. Clones on Orphan Trains into empty cities. Sit with what you missed, then return to the Tartaria deep-dive. The Dark Ages and Industrial Revolution were covers. The 8th Re-set still aims 15-minute cages and FEMA asylums. Discard Religion, Finance, and Perceived Knowledge. Remember the old world before the EMF peels the lie.

questions.question: What was Great Tartary, and how did its end actually occur?

options.label: A
options.text: A globally distributed, highly advanced civilization of aesthetic and technological excellence that was abruptly terminated by a pre-planned Re-set.
options.rationale: Tartaria was world-scale excellence wiped by a planned Re-set; we sit in the 7th cycle toward an 8th.

options.label: B
options.text: A small fishing village that faded slowly through natural economic decline with no Re-set and no global reach.
options.rationale: Great Tartary was a globally distributed advanced civilization terminated by a pre-planned Re-set, not slow natural decline.

options.label: C
options.text: A Freemason brand for coal companies with no free-energy infrastructure and no civilizational architecture.
options.rationale: It was aesthetic and free-energy excellence later dismantled and hidden by parasitic proxies.

options.label: D
options.text: A future project that never existed, invented only by modern internet forums last decade.
options.rationale: Great Tartary existed as a real worldwide civilization erased from modern records by victors.

questions.hint: Global advanced civilization — pre-planned Re-set — seventh cycle now.

questions.question: What roles did the Dark Ages narrative and the Industrial Revolution play relative to Tartaria?

options.label: A
options.text: Both restored Tartarian resonator domes and taught harmonic stone craft, which is why the period produced so many great cathedrals and halls.
options.rationale: Not what the report says. Dark Ages = timeline overwrite; Industrial Revolution = free-energy downgrade cover story.

options.label: B
options.text: The Dark Ages narrative was invented to overwrite Tartaria's timeline, while the Industrial Revolution dismantled and downgraded its free-energy technology.
options.rationale: Dark Ages = timeline overwrite; Industrial Revolution = free-energy downgrade cover story.

options.label: C
options.text: The Dark Ages ended Tartaria by plague, and the Industrial Revolution was a separate economic boom that had no link to its technology.
options.rationale: Not what the report says. Dark Ages = timeline overwrite; Industrial Revolution = free-energy downgrade cover story.

options.label: D
options.text: Both openly celebrated Tartarian free energy, publishing its timelines in schools until the archives were lost in later wars and fires.
options.rationale: Not what the report says. Dark Ages = timeline overwrite; Industrial Revolution = free-energy downgrade cover story.

questions.hint: Dark Ages overwrite timeline — Industrial Revolution downgrades free energy.

questions.question: How was Great Tartary historically divided geographically?

options.label: A
options.text: It had no geographic divisions and never spanned worldwide infrastructure or culture.
options.rationale: Great Tartary was worldwide, historically split East (China) and West (rest of world).

options.label: B
options.text: Into East Tartary (modern China) and West Tartary (the rest of the world).
options.rationale: East Tartary = modern China; West Tartary = rest of world; records erased after Re-set.

options.label: C
options.text: Only into North and South poles with no East/West civilizational split at all.
options.rationale: It was divided into East Tartary (modern China) and West Tartary (the rest of the world).

options.label: D
options.text: Only into city blocks of one capital with no continental or regional naming structure.
options.rationale: Historical division is East Tartary as modern China and West Tartary as the rest of the world.

questions.hint: East Tartary = China; West Tartary = rest of world.

options.label: D
options.text: Random accidents with no orchestration and no thousand-year planning by parasitic forces.
options.rationale: They are orchestrated cyclical events on roughly thousand-year intervals.
